module_title: Physiological Mechanisms: Urine Formation, Muscle Contraction & Nerve Impulses
introduction: This level targets the highly tested step-by-step physiological mechanisms. It details how urine is ultrafiltered and concentrated, the biochemical cycle driving muscle contraction (Sliding Filament Theory), and the electrochemistry behind generating a nerve impulse (Action Potential).

core_concepts.title: Urine Formation
core_concepts.description:
Involves three main processes:
1. Glomerular Filtration: Ultrafiltration of blood through 3 layers (endothelium of blood vessel, epithelium of Bowman's capsule/Podocytes, and basement membrane). Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) is approx. $125 \text{ mL/min}$ ($180 \text{ L/day}$).
2. Reabsorption: Since $180 \text{ L}$ is filtered but only $1.5 \text{ L}$ is excreted, 99% of the filtrate is reabsorbed. Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) reabsorbs 70-80% of electrolytes and water. 
3. Secretion: Tubular cells secrete $H^+, K^+,$ and ammonia into the filtrate to maintain ionic and acid-base balance of body fluids.

core_concepts.title: Muscle Contraction (Sliding Filament Theory)
core_concepts.description:
Proposed by Huxley and Huxley. Contraction occurs by the sliding of thin filaments (Actin) over the thick filaments (Myosin). 
Steps: 
1. Action potential reaches Neuromuscular Junction, releasing Acetylcholine.
2. Action potential spreads into T-tubules, causing Sarcoplasmic Reticulum to release $Ca^{2+}$.
3. $Ca^{2+}$ binds to Troponin on the actin filament, removing the masking of active sites for myosin.
4. Myosin head binds to actin, forming a Cross-Bridge (requires ATP hydrolysis).
5. The myosin head pulls the actin filament towards the center of the A-band (Power stroke), shortening the sarcomere (Z-lines move closer). ATP binding breaks the cross-bridge.

core_concepts.title: Generation & Conduction of Nerve Impulse
core_concepts.description:
1. Resting State: The axonal membrane is more permeable to $K^+$ and nearly impermeable to $Na^+$. The Sodium-Potassium pump actively transports 3 $Na^+$ OUT and 2 $K^+$ IN, maintaining a Resting Membrane Potential of $-70 \text{ mV}$ (inside negative, outside positive).
2. Depolarization: A stimulus opens voltage-gated $Na^+$ channels. $Na^+$ rushes IN rapidly, reversing the polarity (inside becomes positive). This generates an Action Potential ($+30 \text{ mV}$ to $+45 \text{ mV}$).
3. Repolarization: $Na^+$ channels close, $K^+$ channels open. $K^+$ rushes OUT, restoring the resting negative potential.

core_concepts.title: Reflex Action and Synaptic Transmission
core_concepts.description:
A reflex is an involuntary, sudden response to a stimulus. The Reflex Arc pathway: Receptor $\rightarrow$ Afferent (Sensory) Neuron $\rightarrow$ Dorsal root ganglion $\rightarrow$ CNS (Spinal Cord Integration) $\rightarrow$ Efferent (Motor) Neuron $\rightarrow$ Ventral root $\rightarrow$ Effector Organ (Muscle).
Synaptic Transmission occurs via neurotransmitters (like Acetylcholine) crossing the synaptic cleft from the presynaptic membrane to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane.

important_entities.name: The Sarcomere
important_entities.key_fact: The functional unit of muscle contraction.
important_entities.significance: A sarcomere is the portion of a myofibril between two successive Z-lines. During contraction: The I-band gets shorter, the H-zone disappears, but the A-band (thick myosin filaments) strictly RETAINS its length.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In nerve impulse generation, if a stimulus is applied but it fails to depolarize the membrane to the 'Threshold Potential' (usually around $-55 \text{ mV}$), NO action potential will be generated at all. It strictly follows the 'All or None' principle. A stronger stimulus does not produce a 'stronger' action potential; it only increases the FREQUENCY of action potentials.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Cerebrum Thinks, Cerebellum Balances, Medulla Breathes
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
Cerebrum: Memory, intelligence, voluntary actions.
Cerebellum: Posture, balance, and coordination of complex muscular movements.
Medulla Oblongata: Involuntary vital centers (Respiration, Cardiovascular reflexes, Gastric secretions).

exam_strategy_tips: For the eye, remember the exact sequence of cell layers in the Retina from INSIDE (vitreous humor side) to OUTSIDE (choroid side): Ganglion cells $\rightarrow$ Bipolar cells $\rightarrow$ Photoreceptor cells (Rods and Cones). Light enters through the ganglion cells first to reach the photoreceptors.
